topic.label: Observability
topic.desc: Observability of software and agent systems: metrics, logs and traces, instrumentation, dashboards, alerts and SLOs, agent and LLM tracing, root-cause debugging, drift and regression monitoring, incidents and capacity. Extends the base Observability topic, which held Observability and Evaluation.

concepts: The three telemetry signals: what each answers, how to name and label them, sampling and retention.
Adding telemetry to code and pipelines: OpenTelemetry spans, context propagation, collectors and keeping cardinality under control.
Building views that answer questions: choosing charts, queries, panels and layouts for operators and for managers.
Turning signals into pages worth waking up for: service level objectives, error budgets, burn rates, thresholds and alert routing.
Seeing what an agent actually did: traces of model calls, tool calls and handoffs, token and latency cost, prompt versions and user feedback.
Finding why something broke: reading logs and traces, forming and testing hypotheses, bisecting changes and writing the finding down.
Noticing when behaviour changes without a deploy: data and output drift, evaluation sets, regression gates and canary comparisons.
Running an incident and planning capacity: severity, roles, status updates, load, saturation, cost and forecasts.
skills: Says whether a question needs a metric, a log line or a trace and what the cheapest signal that answers it is.
Designs metric names, units and labels that stay consistent and flags labels that would explode the number of series.
Sets how long each signal is kept and how traces are sampled, with the cost and the evidence that is lost at each setting.
Adds spans, attributes and context propagation to a service and checks that a request shows as one connected trace.
Configures receivers, processors and exporters in a collector pipeline and tests that data reaches each backend.
Finds labels and attributes with too many distinct values and proposes bucketing or dropping them before the bill arrives.
Designs a dashboard around the questions an operator asks first, with the golden signals at the top and links to detail.
Writes promql and logql queries over metrics and logs for a stated question and explains what each part of the query filters or aggregates.
Reviews an existing dashboard for panels nobody reads, misleading axes and missing context and lists what to remove.
Defines service level indicators and objectives from user-visible behaviour and sets the error budget and its window.
Writes multi-window burn-rate alerts for an SLO and shows how fast each alert fires for a given outage.
Finds alerts that fire often without action, groups duplicates and proposes thresholds or routes that cut noise safely.
Reads a trace of an agent run and summarises the model calls, tool calls, errors and handoffs in order, with latency for each step.
Breaks token use, latency and spend down by step, tool and prompt version and shows where the money goes.
Ties each run to the prompt, model and tool versions used so a behaviour change can be traced to its cause.
Links user ratings and corrections to the traces that produced them so bad runs can be found and replayed.
Reads logs and stack traces for a failure, extracts the first error and lists what must be checked next.
Forms rival explanations for a failure, picks the cheapest test for each and reports which were ruled out.
Narrows a regression to one change by bisecting versions, flags or configuration and records each step.
Compares current inputs and outputs with a baseline and reports which distributions moved and by how much.
Builds an evaluation set and a pass threshold that blocks a release when quality drops, runs a canary first and records every run.
Compares a canary with the baseline on stated metrics and says whether the difference is larger than noise.
Rates an incident by user impact and spread, names the incident commander and lists who must be told.
Writes short, dated status updates for stakeholders during an incident that say what is known, what is not, what is being done and when the next update comes.
Projects load, saturation and cost from usage trends and says when a limit will be reached and with what margin.
Finds metrics and labels that explode in number, estimates their storage cost and proposes which to drop or aggregate.
Defines log fields, levels and correlation ids so logs can be searched and joined with traces.
Lays out a one-screen view of traffic, errors, latency and saturation with links down to traces and logs.
Designs scripted checks that exercise a user journey on a schedule and decides what a failure should trigger.
Reads a distributed trace, finds the span that dominates latency and says whether it is work, waiting or retries.
Compares log patterns now with a baseline period and lists new, vanished or sharply changed message types.
Writes the incident timeline, contributing causes, what detection missed and the follow-up actions with owners and dates.
